finding.text: The new `ai/AISession` page at 400 is 81% empty (layout.json `empty 0.812`, tab_rows 2) — a thin index page; fine for a readme index, but the Doc tab bar takes two rows at 400.
`drawer-rail-ai` and `mode-btn` report wraps of 1.7–3.2 lines at 400 (layout.json wraps) — shared site chrome (icon-font text), untouched by this diff.
The five class wraps (AICost, EditSwitch, DesignScore, PanelGlyphs, LayoutControls) were not opened headless here; the shims re-export every old name, so only the diff was checked.
`AISession/page.js` `files:` lists 6 of the ~20 files its readme names — readme is the fuller index.

The new `/framework/ai/AISession/` page renders empty: title and two tabs, then blank (empty 82% at 400, 92% at 3440; layout.json `tab-panel` 70px at 400) — shots/127-0-0-1-59502-framework-ai-AISession/sheet.png. Its `Doc` subject is the class `AISession`, but no class card, file tree or demo shows; it fails "show, don't tell" (page 1, content 1) and the readme's list of 15 classes is not visible on the page.

Ask 2 (top five become classes) — shown in the diff as five shims (`cost.js` is 4 lines) and five class files, but "tests green", "pages opened headless" and "one commit each" are not visible in the diff or shots; only the log line claims it.

Ask 1 wants a Haiku-named class and API for the top 20; ranks 12, 13 and 18 in the census are still "name to confirm", and items 21–40 carry no API. Ask 1's "rule it breaks, one line each" is stated once at the top, not per row.

The census page is not linked from the AI readme chain's own index beyond one architecture.md heading and one patterns readme bullet; both exist, so it meets the "one readme line" fence, but the page is reachable only through code/patterns/readme.md (not a `children:` change) — confirm it appears under the Patterns Docs tab.

Review was run `light` (decision logged), widths given: all four (400, 1200, 1920, 3440) for `/framework/ai/` and `/framework/ai/AISession/`; the pre-existing `drawer-rail-ai` / `drawer-rail-menu` buttons wrap to 3.2 lines at 400 (layout.json wraps), not caused by this diff.

The new `/framework/ai/AISession/` page shows only its title and tabs; the readme body is not visible at any width (empty 82% at 400, 84% at 1200, 89% at 1920, 92% at 3440; items 9) — `shots/127-0-0-1-59502-framework-ai-AISession/sheet.png`. The `page.js` fetches `readme.md` after an await, so either the md never rendered or the shot was taken before it did. Open it headless and wait for the body before landing.
Requirement 4 asks for `code/patterns/doc/oo-census.md`; it is in the diff but not on disk in the main tree I read, so I judged it from the patch only. Confirm it lands.

The diff is a mix: the five classes (AICost, EditSwitch, DesignScore, PanelGlyphs, LayoutControls) plus an unrelated AISession page and readme. I did not check that these match the brief's ranking. The requirements ask for a Haiku-named top 20; I could not see that evidence in the diff.
Only the `/framework/ai/` and `AISession` pages were shot. The pages that import the five new classes (Ask, DesignTool, Panel, layout) were not shot, so "pages opened headless" is unverified.

Ask 2 said "under about 10 callers each"; the five classes have 10, 13, 10, 12 and 21 importers (oo-census.md table). `ext/Ask/edit.js` at 21 is double the limit. Shims keep it safe, but the brief's limit was passed without a stated reason.
Ask 1 wanted a Haiku pass naming the class and API for the top 20. Rows 12, 13, 33, 35-40 say "name to confirm", and no row lists an API. Only the "Should be" column is filled.
Ask 3 says ten modules, but the spot-check table has eleven rows (`ai/AISession` was added to the ten). The count is off by one, and the card title "10 modules spot-checked" needs the same fix.

The AISession page shows its title twice: page-title "AISession", then the readme's h1 "AISession — one Claude session as a class family". At 400 that h1 wraps to 4 lines (layout.json wraps, h1 lines 4). It is readable, so this is not a fix.
Only `AISession` has shots. The five class changes are not pages, so n/a for them. The diff did not show callers rewritten by `RenameScript`; I could not verify this from the patch.
